Summary: Evan Buckley knew he had never belonged to the Buckleys; something inside him said he wasn't part of that family. Maybe it was the toy fire truck he held in his hand, which he had always had and remembered, that whispered there was something more he didn't know could exist. The initials carved into the truck, R. N., made him wish he knew what they meant. Perhaps, in time, he could find himself. Bobby Nash wanted to be angry, but what he really felt was worry. Buck was always reckless, rebellious, and never took care of himself, which terrified Bobby. He wanted to protect him, not knowing if the real reason was because he saw Buck in the little boy he lost years ago, or perhaps the mark that looked so much like his baby son's—though he knew it could just be a coincidence, because that's how things happened: coincidences.
